renderings.prompt: Wide cinematic Minecraft voxel render of a downtown Houston cityscape at golden hour. Glass and steel office towers of varying heights — including a 1980s granite-and-glass tower, a tall tapered I.M. Pei-style tower, two dark mirrored Philip Johnson trapezoidal towers, and a pair of cream Art Deco twin towers with stepped parapets. Surface streets with palm trees, parking garages, glass skybridges connecting upper floors across streets, yellow centerlines on gray asphalt, hot sunny climate, light beige sidewalks. Blocky pixelated Minecraft geometry rendered in cinematic 4K detail, voxel aesthetic visible. Wide panoramic.
renderings.intended_use: Master plan section 1 (Above-ground city) — opening spread

renderings.prompt: Street-level Minecraft voxel render of the Wells Fargo Plaza office tower entrance in downtown Houston, 1980s architectural style. Granite and glass facade, polished andesite plaza at the corner, a small blue T-marker plaque set into the stone-brick sidewalk, glass revolving door, an almost-secret feel. The building rises behind, off-white quartz walls with light-gray stained-glass window panes. Hot sunny day, palm tree casting a long shadow, light beige sidewalks.
renderings.intended_use: Master plan section 2 (The entrance paradox — Wells Fargo direct entry)

renderings.prompt: Street-level Minecraft voxel render of a 1970s open-deck concrete parking garage in downtown Houston. The McKinney Garage on Main Street. Gray concrete structure, multi-level open decks visible, ground-floor retail concourse with small storefronts, a T-marker plaque on the sidewalk, a Tunnel Level sign with an arrow pointing down, a stairway descending. Different feel from a polished office-tower lobby — this is utilitarian, parking-garage-with-shops. Hot sunny day, light beige sidewalks, palm trees.
renderings.intended_use: Master plan section 2 (The other direct entry — McKinney Garage)

renderings.prompt: Interior Minecraft voxel render of a 1980s office-tower lobby descending to a basement tunnel. Polished andesite and marble floor, quartz-pillar columns, a bank of iron-block elevator doors, an interior stair of polished-andesite stairs with a dark-oak-fence handrail going down. The lobby is warm and grand, lit by redstone lamp chandeliers; the basement below is fluorescent, cool, off-white painted concrete walls, sea-lantern ceiling lights. The visual contrast between the marble lobby and the beige tunnel below.
renderings.intended_use: Master plan section 3 (The descent — lobby to basement transition)

renderings.prompt: The signature image. A long straight Minecraft voxel render of a typical 1970s-Hines-era underground pedestrian tunnel corridor in Houston. Off-white white-concrete walls, smooth-stone-slab dropped acoustic-tile ceiling in a 2x4 grid pattern, beige white-wool VCT floor, fluorescent sea-lantern strip lights every 4 blocks, a single backlit blue-terracotta wayfinding band sign at the far end reading Tunnel with an arrow. The corridor is 3 blocks wide and 3 blocks tall, low ceiling, beige, climate-controlled, no daylight. A few small tenant signage accents on the walls.
renderings.intended_use: Master plan section 4 (The standard corridor — hero shot)

renderings.prompt: Minecraft voxel render of the Esperson food court in the Houston tunnel system. The archetype. A long, narrow corridor with a single row of small storefronts on each side. Off-white dropped ceiling with fluorescent sea-lantern tubes, beige polished-andesite terrazzo floor, off-white painted concrete-block walls. A backlit blue wayfinding band sign at a midpoint. Storefronts include a Chick-fil-A red awning, a Mediterranean counter, a kolache shop, a coffee kiosk, with iron-bars storefront frames and glass-pane windows. Dark-oak-slab communal tables with dark-oak-fence bases. A few office-worker silhouettes walking. The lunch-rush feel.
renderings.intended_use: Master plan section 5 (The food court — Esperson archetype)

renderings.prompt: Minecraft voxel render of the Pennzoil Place underground food court in the Houston tunnel system. The densest. A wider node with 10-12 tightly packed storefronts, minimal aisle space, dark ceiling accents, kitchen-exhaust iron-trapdoor grilles overhead. Two dark Philip Johnson mirrored trapezoidal towers visible through glass-pane at the corridor end. Storefronts include Chick-fil-A red, Which Wich black and orange, Salata red-orange, Treebeards brown, Otto's BBQ red and black, Michael's Cookie Jar brown. Packed, crowded, no clear aisle.
renderings.intended_use: Master plan section 5 (The food court — Pennzoil densest)

renderings.prompt: Minecraft voxel render of the 1001 Fannin Lamar Tunnel food court in Houston. The modern refresh. Dark gray and black concrete dropped ceiling, polished dark-charcoal gray-wool and black-concrete floor, frameless glass-pane storefronts, end-rod and redstone-lamp LED panel lighting strips. Storefronts include Blackwater Coffee black and cream, Charlies BBQ red, Baoz Dumplings cyan, Lenny's Grill orange, Red's Barber red-white-blue barber pole, Addict Tea white. Clean, contemporary, 2020s minimalist. Sharp contrast to the 1970s Esperson food court.
renderings.intended_use: Master plan section 5 (The food court — 1001 Fannin modern refresh)

renderings.prompt: Minecraft voxel render of the McKinney Place 930 Main concourse food court in Houston. A long linear concourse under an open-deck parking garage above. Gray concrete ceiling with exposed iron-block ductwork, beige and gray-wool floor. Storefronts include Sparkle Dry Cleaners light-blue and white, Shipley's Do-nuts pink and white, Renato Jewelers gold, Taka Sushi white, a barber pole with red-white-blue stripes, Mayuri Express orange. A few office-worker silhouettes. More utilitarian, less polished than Esperson or 1001 Fannin. Parking-garage-food-court feel.
renderings.intended_use: Master plan section 5 (The food court — McKinney public entry)

renderings.prompt: Minecraft voxel render of a Houston above-ground glass skybridge crossing McKinney Street at the second-floor level. Glass-pane curtain walls with iron-bars brushed-aluminum mullions, white-wool carpet floor, quartz-slab acoustic-tile ceiling, soft redstone-lamp LED lighting. The street visible below with a small white van and a single pedestrian on a smooth-stone-slab sidewalk. The two connected office towers flank the bridge — one a glass-and-steel 1980s tower, the other a similar 1990s tower. Hot sunny sky with palm-tree shadows.
renderings.intended_use: Master plan section 7 (The skywalk network)

renderings.prompt: Close-up Minecraft voxel render of a small brass T-marker surface entrance plaque set into a stone-brick sidewalk at the curb of Louisiana Street in downtown Houston, outside the Wells Fargo Plaza tower. The marker is a small blue T inside a circle on an oak-sign, easy to miss, inlaid into light-gray-concrete sidewalk. The granite-and-glass base of the Wells Fargo tower is visible in the soft-focus background. Hot sunny day, a palm-tree shadow across the sidewalk, the moment of discovery.
renderings.intended_use: Master plan section 2 (The T-marker easter egg)

renderings.prompt: Three-panel Minecraft voxel render composition showing the time-staggered wayfinding system in the Houston tunnel. Left: a 1970s blue-terracotta backlit band sign with white-concrete Tunnel arrow text, slightly yellowed, mounted on off-white tunnel walls. Center: a 1990s cleaner version, white-on-blue, less yellowed, with a building name. Right: a 2010s minimal version, white text on black-concrete with a single end-rod arrow. The chronic weak point of the real system. The three eras of commercial signage side by side.
renderings.intended_use: Master plan section 8 (The wayfinding system — time-staggered)

renderings.prompt: Minecraft voxel render of the Wells Fargo floodgate at the tunnel-level entry. A vertical iron-block door slotted into iron-block brackets, with a small oak-sign plaque reading Floodgate — Tropical Storm Allison, June 2001. A sump-pump utility room visible through an open side door, with a cauldron and iron-bars piping. A 6-inch raised stone-brick-stairs threshold at the doorway. The off-white 1970s tunnel corridor continues beyond. The engineering easter egg that distinguishes the Houston tunnel from a generic underground concourse.
renderings.intended_use: Master plan section 9 (Flood-control — Tropical Storm Allison)

renderings.prompt: Close-up Minecraft voxel render of a bronze wall plaque in the Wells Fargo Plaza lobby. The plaque reads: Houston Tunnel System — Established 1930s. First tunnel: Ross Sterling under Fannin 1931 and Will Horwitz under Capitol 1935. Inspired by the Rockefeller Center underground concourse. Mounted on a polished-andesite lobby wall next to a quartz-pillar column. Soft redstone-lamp accent lighting from above. A polished-andesite floor and a building-directory item-frame array visible in soft focus behind.
renderings.intended_use: Master plan section 10 (The 1930s dual-origin story)

renderings.prompt: Minecraft voxel render of the 200000 daily users interpretive panel in the Wells Fargo Plaza lobby. A small footnote: Back-of-envelope estimate from daytime downtown workforce. Mounted on a polished-andesite wall above a quartz-slab bench. Soft redstone-lamp accent lighting from above.
renderings.intended_use: Master plan section 10 (The 200,000 lore easter egg)

Mounted on a light-gray-concrete wall next to a Salata red-orange storefront with iron-bars frame and glass-pane window. A small fluorescent sea-lantern above.
renderings.intended_use: Master plan section 10 (The 'largest' lore with correction)

renderings.prompt: Wide panoramic Minecraft voxel render of the combined-complex layout at golden hour. In the foreground, a downtown Houston CBD with skyscrapers in a valley — the Wells Fargo glass-and-granite tower, JPMorgan Chase tapered tower, Pennzoil mirrored trapezoids, Esperson Art Deco twin towers, with palm-tree-lined streets and parking garages. Behind it on the north side, a tall mountain range with the Cheyenne Mountain Complex nestled into the rock face, an entrance portal visible. On the south side across a flatter coastal plain, the SubTropolis industrial complex with massive loading-dock doors. Warm late-afternoon sky, voxel geometry, cinematic Minecraft aesthetic.
renderings.intended_use: Master plan combined report (cross-build spread)

renderings.prompt: Minecraft voxel render of a 3/4 cutaway view of the entire Houston tunnel-system build. The above-ground city on top — skyscrapers, parking garages, skybridges, palm-tree-lined streets, hot sunny climate. Below, the underground tunnel system — a 4x6 block grid of corridors and 4 food-court nodes at the same horizontal positions as the above-ground anchors. The vertical cross-section shows the relationship between street level, the skybridge level at the second floor, and the tunnel level 20 feet below grade. Subtle soft technical annotations. The shadow city made literal.
renderings.intended_use: Master plan section 11 (Two-layer integration cutaway)

renderings.prompt: Four-panel Minecraft voxel render composition of the Houston tunnel at different times of day. Top-left lunch rush: fluorescent-lit, packed with office-worker silhouettes, brand colors pop, the food court vibrant. Top-right mid-afternoon: dimmer, half-empty, fluorescent, calm, a few workers. Bottom-left after-hours: lights off except a few dim sea-lanterns, cleaning-crew silhouettes with iron-bars carts, a security-locked iron-block elevator bank, a small Tunnel Closed 6 PM oak-sign. Bottom-right weekend morning: dark, climate-controlled, unstaffed, the same corridor space feeling completely empty.

renderings.prompt: Minecraft voxel render of the Niels Esperson Art Deco twin towers in downtown Houston, viewed from the sidewalk. The two towers of different heights, classic 1930s Art Deco silhouette. Hot sunny day, palm tree at the corner, a glass skybridge connecting to a neighboring tower at the second floor.
